Test rumble
Getting started

1. On your PC, install TunaStream and keep it running. Its icon sits by the clock.

2. Connect this device to the same network as the PC, by cable or 5 GHz Wi-Fi if you can.

3. Your PC appears here by itself. If it doesn't, choose Add PC Manually and type the address shown on TunaStream's home page.

4. Choose the PC. A PIN appears: on the PC, open TunaStream, go to the PIN page, enter it and press Send.

5. Choose a game. It opens on its own screen on the PC, sized for this TV.
If something isn\'t working

The PC doesn't show up: check that TunaStream is running and both are on the same network (guest Wi-Fi usually blocks this). Or choose Add PC Manually and type the address from TunaStream's home page.

Pairing fails: enter the PIN on TunaStream's PIN page within a minute or so, then try again.

The picture stutters: in this PC's menu, choose Fit picture quality to this connection. A cable, or 5 GHz Wi-Fi, helps most. Picture quality and size also adjust themselves while you play; afterwards, How the last stream went in the PC's menu says what happened.

The TV feels slow to respond: turn on auto low latency mode (ALLM) in the TV's HDMI settings so it switches to game mode by itself, or choose its Game mode by hand.

No rumble: on the PC, open TunaStream's Troubleshooting page during a stream and press Rumble now. If the controller buzzes, the game needs its vibration turned on; if not, check Rumble in this app's Settings.

The game opens on the PC's monitor: update TunaStream from its home page; it moves the game onto the stream's screen.

More help is on TunaStream's Help page on the PC.

Adjust picture quality to the Wi-Fi
Watches how each frame arrives. When the Wi-Fi is getting full, it softens the picture a little before anything stutters, then goes back to full quality.
Adjust picture size too

When the Wi-Fi drops a long way, send a smaller picture and let the TV stretch it, which looks cleaner than a blocky full-size one. It goes back to full size by itself. Needs Adjust picture quality to the Wi-Fi.
Test a smaller picture (10 seconds)
Sending a smaller picture for 10 seconds. It should stay full-screen, look a little softer, then sharpen again.
Can\'t try that here. Turn on both Adjust options in Settings, and update TunaStream on the PC.
Switch the TV to game mode
While a game is on screen, ask the TV to skip its picture processing, which takes away a lot of delay. The TV goes back to normal afterwards. Needs a TV with auto low latency mode (ALLM).
10-bit picture (experimental)
Smoother colour gradients and slightly better use of the Wi-Fi, without HDR. Turn off if games show a black or green picture.
Reconnect by itself
If a stream drops mid-game, start it again automatically. The game keeps running on the PC meanwhile.

How big is the picture?
Let\'s set TunaReceive up for this TV. It takes a minute, and you can change anything later in Settings.\n\nTunaStream gives each stream its own screen on the PC at exactly this size.
4K
3840 × 2160. The sharpest, and needs a strong connection.
2560 × 1440. Sharper than 1080p, lighter than 4K.
1920 × 1080. The best fit for most Wi-Fi.
1280 × 720. For a weak connection.
How smooth?
This screen can show up to 120 frames a second. 120 feels smoother in fast games, and the PC has to render twice as many frames.
120 frames a second
Smoothest. Best on a wired connection or strong 5 GHz Wi-Fi.
60 frames a second
Smooth, and easy on the PC and the connection.
Smoother or sharper?
%1$s\n\nStutter on a clean connection usually means the picture is asking for slightly more than the Wi-Fi can carry, so leave some headroom.
